title: The String constant pool
context: What is the String constant pool for?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java basics questions (2 of 3)
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: The String constant pool is a special area of the heap where the JVM stores one copy of each distinct string literal. When two literals have the same text, they refer to the same object. `intern()` puts a string into the pool and returns the pooled copy. The pool saves memory and makes `==` work for literals, although you should still use equals to compare content.

points.title: One copy per literal
points.why: Literals with the same text share one object, which saves memory.

points.title: Don't rely on == for content
points.why: Strings built at run time are not pooled, so == gives false even when the text matches.
